content.comment_body: I am looking to send an SMS to my [product_name] [product_name] module to activate an output. While it's documented that the module can send and receive SMS messages, the manual provides minimal information regarding SMS formatting or the actions that can result from a received SMS—only brief sentences about configuring contacts and troubleshooting connection issues. I am able to send SMS messages triggered by events in the [product_name] module, but I cannot initiate events in the module upon receiving SMS. My setup utilizes [article_no], which only supports [version_no] communication. I've attempted approaches similar to another communication module but without success, as this module lacks certain features. I tried different methods, including having the module function as either server or client. Does anyone know if the SMS text needs a specific format? I've attached my current setup for review—any insight on potential errors or misconfiguration is welcome.

Hello [user_name], Based on my experience, here’s how to configure SMS messaging: 1) Establish an [version_no] client connection in [product_name] with the required tag. 2) Enable the protocol via the menu—review log configuration and confirm the server connection with the device’s IP address, then save changes. 3) Create a recipient phone number through the contacts menu and add the desired entry, saving once done. 4) Set up an activation label in data management, assigning a symbolic name and label. 5) Define your SMS text under the messages section, specifying both symbol and content and saving. 6) Activate SMS by adding a new line under data connections, choosing to send to the correct recipient upon a positive label edge, then activate and save. [Images referenced in the original post]

Thank you for your time and help. In an earlier topic about [product_name] mapping, I tried your approach. [user_name] previously provided a link to an FAQ that matched your instructions, though your images were much clearer. Through multiple experiments and the FAQ post, I managed to receive SMS messages based on events in the [product_name] module. However, I was unable to send SMS messages to the communication interface to trigger actions. That’s why I’m seeking more specific help here. After much trial and error, I eventually achieved the intended result; oddly, the attached documentation I previously created does work now. I’ve since tested this with a new program and shared another document for review. The solution operates correctly, but any feedback or suggestions are welcome. Thanks to everyone who assisted.
Thank you very much for your input, [user_name]!

One additional point: Any digital bit you want to control externally (via SMS or panel) works only if it is not managed by your [product_name] program. If the output is used in your program, outside control is disabled because the program always takes priority.

I'm also unable to modify a variable using a received SMS. I can send SMS via the [product_name] module and observe variable changes between the interface and the module. Communication between them appears functional, but I’m unable to trigger events within the communication interface using SMS. Any advice on enabling this functionality would be appreciated. I am currently awaiting a response from [company_name] technical support.
Some time ago, I received training documents for the communication interface module. Hopefully, these are useful.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are trying to remotely control outputs on a [product_name] module by sending SMS messages through a communication interface. The primary obstacle is insufficient documentation on SMS formatting and module setup for incoming SMS-triggered events. Although one user eventually succeeded after extensive experimentation, the process remains unclear and confusing for others. Further clarification reveals that outputs managed by the module's internal program cannot be overridden by external SMS or panel commands—program logic holds precedence. Several users request guidance from technical support and the community.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect detailed guidance on formatting SMS commands and configuring the system to reliably trigger outputs via received SMS messages. They seek smoother remote control integration, matching the convenience and reliability of locally-triggered SMS functionality.
